z11_1918.title: Zákon č. 11/1918 Sb., o zřízení samostatného státu československého
z11_1918.note: Act of the National Committee of 28 October 1918, publicly proclaimed and in force that day: 'Samostatný stát československý vstoupil v život.'

uz542_1992.title: Zákon č. 542/1992 Sb., o zániku České a Slovenské Federativní Republiky
uz542_1992.note: Constitutional act of 25 November 1992: the federation ceased to exist at the end of 31 December 1992, and its powers passed to the Czech Republic and the Slovak Republic on 1 January 1993 (arts. 1, 2); arts. 4 made the deputies elected in 1992 to the Federal Assembly and the national councils the legislatures of the successor states.

z123_1920.title: Zákon č. 123/1920 Sb., kterým vydává se řád volení do poslanecké sněmovny.
z123_1920.note: Election law of the Chamber of Deputies, 29 February 1920: 23 electoral regions (volební kraje) electing 300 deputies by list PR (art. I); the first election excluded regions 22 (Těšín) and 23 (Subcarpathian Rus), Hlučín, Vitorazsko, Valtice, and the Spiš and Orava plebiscite areas, whose deputies were to be elected later (art. II).

z124_1920.title: Zákon č. 124/1920 Sb., o složení a pravomoci senátu.
z124_1920.note: The Senate: 150 elected members (§ 1), elected under the Chamber's election law (§ 2) by voters aged 26 and over (§ 3), for eight years (§ 5).

ns1920.title: Volby do Národního shromáždění 1920 až 1935
ns1920.license: ČSÚ terms of use: reuse with attribution to the Czech Statistical Office

d47_1945.title: Ústavní dekret č. 47/1945 Sb., o Prozatímním Národním shromáždění
d47_1945.note: Presidential constitutional decree of 25 August 1945: a single chamber of 300 members to sit until a Constituent National Assembly elected by universal, equal, direct, and secret ballot under PR; its members were chosen indirectly under a government order.

uz65_1946.title: Ústavní zákon č. 65/1946 Sb., o ústavodárném Národním shromáždění
uz65_1946.note: Constitutional act of 11 April 1946 on the Constituent National Assembly of 300 members.

z67_1946.title: Zákon č. 67/1946 Sb., o volbě ústavodárného Národního shromáždění
z67_1946.note: Election law of the Constituent National Assembly: 28 electoral regions (§ 1), list PR with seats apportioned among the Czech land, the Moravian-Silesian land, and Slovakia (§ 2).

uz74_1948.title: Ústavní zákon č. 74/1948 Sb., jímž se na přechodnou dobu do účinnosti nové ústavy upravuje volba a pravomoc Národního shromáždění a činnost Ústavodárného Národního shromáždění
uz74_1948.note: Constitutional act of 16 April 1948: a National Assembly of one chamber of 300 members with a six-year term (art. 1), elected by PR (art. 2).

z75_1948.title: Zákon č. 75/1948 Sb., o volbách do Národního shromáždění
z75_1948.note: Election law of 1948: electoral regions grouped into two electoral areas, regions 1 to 19 (Czech lands) and 20 to 28 (Slovakia) (§ 1), 300 deputies (§ 2); the minister of the interior called the election in the Official Gazette (§ 22).

u150_1948.title: Ústavní zákon č. 150/1948 Sb., Ústava Československé republiky
u150_1948.note: Constitution of 9 May 1948: a National Assembly of one chamber of 300 members elected for six years; the President elected by it for seven years.

z14_1954.title: Zákon č. 14/1954 Sb., o volbách do národních výborů
z14_1954.note: First election law of the regional, district, and local national committees, members elected in single-member constituencies.

z27_1954.title: Zákon č. 27/1954 Sb., o volbách do Národního shromáždění
z27_1954.note: Election law of 26 May 1954: one deputy in each single-member constituency (§ 3), one constituency for every 35,000 inhabitants (§ 4).

uz35_1960.title: Ústavní zákon č. 35/1960 Sb., o změně ústavního zákona o volbách do Národního shromáždění a o volbách do Slovenské národní rady a ústavního zákona o národních výborech
uz35_1960.note: Fixed 300 constituencies for the National Assembly (art. I § 1); the Slovak National Council used the Slovak ones.

z39_1960.title: Zákon č. 39/1960 Sb., o volbách do národních výborů

u100_1960.title: Ústavní zákon č. 100/1960 Sb., Ústava Československé socialistické republiky
u100_1960.note: Art. 39: the National Assembly of 300 deputies elected for four years; art. 43: it elects the President; art. 63: by three-fifths of all deputies, for five years.

u37_1964.title: Usnesení č. 37/1964 Sb., o vyhlášení dne voleb do Národního shromáždění, do Slovenské národní rady, do národních výborů a voleb soudců okresních soudů
u37_1964.note: Resolution of the Presidium of the National Assembly calling the National Assembly, Slovak National Council, and national committee elections, and the elections of district court judges, for Sunday 14 June 1964.

uzfed.title: Ústavní zákon č. 143/1968 Sb., o československé federaci

z44_1971.title: Zákon č. 44/1971 Sb., o volbách do Federálního shromáždění
z44_1971.note: Election law of 6 July 1971: 200 constituencies for the House of the People and 150 for the House of the Nations, 75 in each republic (§ 11); one deputy per constituency (§ 10).

uz43_1971.title: Ústavní zákon č. 43/1971 Sb., kterým se mění čl. 86 Ústavy a čl. 30 a 103 ústavního zákona o československé federaci
uz43_1971.note: Lengthened the term of the House of the People, the national councils, and the national committees from four to five years from the general elections of November 1971.

u10_1986.title: Usnesení PŘEDSEDNICTVA FEDERÁLNÍHO SHROMÁŽDĚNÍ, Československé socialistické republiky č. 10/1986 Sb., o vyhlášení voleb do Federálního shromáždění Československé socialistické republiky

uz14_1990.title: Ústavní zákon č. 14/1990 Sb., o odvolávání poslanců zastupitelských sborů a volbě nových poslanců národních výborů
uz14_1990.note: Constitutional act of 23 January 1990: parties recalled deputies of the Federal Assembly, the national councils, and the national committees, and the vacant seats were filled by co-option on the proposal of Civic Forum and Public Against Violence.

uz45_1990.title: Ústavní zákon č. 45/1990 Sb., o zkrácení volebního období zákonodárných sborů
uz45_1990.note: Ended the term of the bodies elected in 1986 at the 1990 election and set the term of the Federal Assembly elected in 1990 at 24 months.

uz327_1991.title: Ústavní zákon č. 327/1991 Sb., o referendu
uz327_1991.note: Constitutional act of 18 July 1991: a referendum on the form of the federation, called by the President in both republics, and the only way for a republic to leave it (art. 1); none was called before the federation was dissolved by constitutional act.

classes.name: Revoluční národní shromáždění 1918–1920
classes.disposition_reason: The provisional legislature was formed from the National Committee, its seats shared among the Czech and Slovak parties by agreement in proportion to the 1911 Imperial Council vote; nobody voted for it.
classes.note: Sat from 14 November 1918 until the first parliamentary election; it adopted the 1920 Constitutional Charter and the election laws, and chose the first President.

classes.name: Volby do poslanecké sněmovny Národního shromáždění
classes.name_en: Chamber of Deputies of the National Assembly
classes.finest_note: ČSÚ republishes totals by electoral region and land; results by district or municipality are only in the printed State Statistical Office volumes.
classes.note: 300 deputies elected by list PR in 23 electoral regions with second and third scrutinies at the national level (Act 123/1920). The 1920 election left out the Těšín region (22), whose territory was split with Poland in July 1920, and Subcarpathian Rus (23), which elected its 9 deputies on 16 March 1924; from 1925 elections were held in 22 regions. The chamber elected in 1935 sat until the occupation of March 1939.

classes.note: 1948: 300 deputies on National Front lists in 28 electoral regions (Act 75/1948). From 1954 one deputy per single-member constituency, one for each 35,000 inhabitants (Act 27/1954); 300 constituencies from 1960 (Constitutional Act 35/1960 and the 1960 Constitution). Slovak National Council and national committee elections were held on the same days in 1954 (national committees on 16 May), 1960, and 1964.

classes.name: Volby do Sněmovny lidu Federálního shromáždění
classes.name_en: Federal Assembly: House of the People
classes.finest_note: For 1990 and 1992 volby.cz gives the Czech part by municipality; the Slovak part survives online only as the federal totals in the gazette and press. The single-list elections of 1971 to 1986 have no published constituency returns.
classes.note: 200 deputies elected across the federation (Constitutional Act 143/1968, art. 30): in single-member constituencies on single lists from 1971 to 1986 (Act 44/1971), then 150 deputies by list PR with a 5% threshold in 12 electoral regions, 8 Czech and 4 Slovak, in 1990 and 1992 (Act 47/1990), each republic's share set by population. Its members of January 1969 were delegated by the old National Assembly, and its 1990 vacancies were filled by co-option (see fs_kooptace). The 1990 term was cut to two years (Constitutional Act 45/1990).

classes.name: Delegování (1969) a kooptace (1990) poslanců Federálního shromáždění
classes.name_en: Federal Assembly members delegated in 1969 and co-opted in 1990
classes.disposition_reason: Seats filled without a vote of the electorate: in January 1969 the House of the People was formed from the National Assembly and the House of the Nations was elected by the Czech and Slovak National Councils from their members (Constitutional Act 143/1968, art. 147); in January and February 1990 recalled deputies were replaced by co-option (Constitutional Act 14/1990).

classes.name: Volba prezidenta republiky
classes.note: The President was always elected by the legislature: the National Assembly in joint session of both chambers for seven years under the 1920 Charter, the National Assembly for seven years under the 1948 Constitution and for five years under the 1960 Constitution, and the Federal Assembly from 1969 (Constitutional Act 143/1968). In July 1992 the Federal Assembly failed in several ballots to elect a successor to Havel, who resigned on 20 July 1992; the office stayed vacant until the federation ended.

classes.name: Referendum o státoprávním uspořádání
classes.name_en: Referendum on the form of the federation
classes.note: Constitutional Act 327/1991 allowed a federation-wide or single-republic referendum on the form of the state, called by the President on the proposal of the Federal Assembly or a national council; none was called before the Federal Assembly dissolved the federation by Constitutional Act 542/1992. No other referendum was provided for between 1918 and 1991.

classes.name: Volby do zemských zastupitelstev
classes.name_en: Land assemblies (Bohemia, Moravia-Silesia, Slovakia, Subcarpathian Rus)
classes.disposition_reason: The returns were printed by the State Statistical Office in 1929 and 1936; no official digital edition was found on csu.gov.cz or volby.statistics.sk.
classes.note: The land administration of 1928 (Act 125/1927) gave each of the four lands an assembly, two-thirds elected by list PR and one-third appointed by the government, elected on 2 December 1928 with the district assemblies and on 26 May 1935, a week after the parliamentary election. The four lands were the groupings ČSÚ uses for the parliamentary returns.

classes.name: Volby do Sněmu Slovenské krajiny (1938) a Sněmu Podkarpatské Rusi (1939)
classes.name_en: Diets of the autonomous Slovak Land (1938) and Carpathian Ukraine (1939)
classes.disposition_reason: Single-list elections of the Second Republic; no official digital publication of the returns was found.
classes.note: The constitutional acts on the autonomy of Slovakia (299/1938) and Subcarpathian Rus (328/1938) of 22 November 1938 created land diets: the Slovak diet of 63 deputies was elected on a single list on 18 December 1938, and the diet of Carpatho-Ukraine on 12 February 1939. The Slovak diet later sat as the parliament of the Slovak State, which the Slovak census covers.

classes.name_en: Municipal councils of the First Republic
classes.disposition_reason: Municipal returns were kept by the municipalities and printed only in part by the State Statistical Office; no official digital edition was found.
classes.note: Councils elected by list PR under the municipal election law of 31 January 1919 (Act 75/1919), first in Bohemia, Moravia, and Silesia on 15 June 1919; Slovakia and Subcarpathian Rus voted later, and municipalities held further elections at the end of each term (1923, 1927, 1931, and 1938 in most of the country) and after dissolutions.

classes.name: Volby do národních výborů 1954–1986
classes.disposition_reason: Single-list elections; only national totals were printed, and no official digital edition of the returns was found.
classes.note: Regional, district, town, and local national committees were elected together in single-member constituencies on National Front lists: under federal laws (14/1954, 39/1960, 34/1964) and from 1971 under laws of the Czech and Slovak National Councils (54/1971, 56/1971). Vacancies went to by-elections called by the presidia. The councils elected in November 1990 under the republics' municipal laws belong to the Czech and Slovak censuses.
